paragraphs.text: Aetherdrift is the 103rd Magic: The Gathering expansion and was released on February 14, 2025 . It features a multiplanar twist on the racing genre: a race across the planes of Avishkar , Amonkhet , and Muraganda . It makes heavy use of Vehicles and Mounts and features the start your engines! , exhaust , and cycling mechanics. The ten Limited archetypes are creatively represented by ten different racing teams from across the Multiverse . The story follows Chandra Nalaar , who hopes to finish first and win the Aetherspark for Nissa Revane .

Aetherdrift contains 291 regular cards (91 commons, 100 uncommons, 60 rares, 20 mythic rares, 20 basic lands) , and includes randomly inserted traditional foil versions of all cards. It is available in Play Boosters , Collector Boosters , two Commander decks , the Aetherdrift Bundle and the special "Finish Line" Bundle.
The related non-Standard code is DRC ( Aetherdrift Commander ); these cards are legal in Commander , Legacy , and Vintage , and reprints remain legal where already legal.

Aetherdrift features 10 Special Guests . These may be found in Play Boosters and may be played in Limited games. You'll find a non-foil Special Guests card in 1 out of 64 Play Boosters (1.5%). Traditional foil Special Guests cards can be found in Collector Boosters (4.2% to replace the traditional foil Booster Fun rare or mythic rare card). The Special Guests for this set have cards and illustrations hand-picked by the Secret Lair team. These unique treatments are designed to embody the multiplanar chaos of Aetherdrift .

Aetherdrift features 10 Japan Showcase cards (DFT #397-416). Each card has been reimagined by Japanese artists and illustrators and has a special frame and style that pays homage to Japanese hobby shops. Unlike Special Guests they use the standard Aetherdrift set code and expansion symbol ( ). Japan Showcase cards appear only in Collector Boosters . In Japanese Collector Boosters, Japan Showcase cards will always be in Japanese. In non-Japanese Collector Boosters, they will appear in English two-thirds of the time and in Japanese one-third of the time. One-in-ten Collector Boosters will have a Japan Showcase card (9% traditional foil, 1% fracture foil).

Play Boosters may contain DFT #1–375 and SPG #84–93. A foil mythic borderless Graffiti Giants card appears in <1% of the boosters. Collector Boosters may contain DFT #1–276, #292–416; #DRC 1–4, DRC #21–36 and SPG #84–93. Japan Showcase cards and Serialized Aethersparks appear in <1% of Collector Boosters. First-place foils appear only in Box Topper packs, which are included in Aetherdrift Play Booster boxes, Collector Booster boxes, and Finish Line Bundles.

The booster box for Play Boosters is reduced from 36 to 30 boosters. Wizards of the Coast also removed the ad card as an option from the 15 card slot; Play Boosters only contain token, emblem, helper, and art cards.

The special "Finish Line" Edition of the Bundle consists of two Collector Boosters and six Play Boosters. It includes five full-art "Driver's Seat" basic lands in " first-place foil ". It also includes one "first-place" foil Box Topper pack, five mana symbol stickers (one for each color), a checkered flag oversized spindown life counter , and three extended alternate art Bundle promo cards (DFT #424–426).

Aetherdrift Booster boxes each include a 2-card Box Topper pack containing 1 of 10 " first-place foil " full-art basic lands and 1 of 127 first-place foil cards from either the main Aetherdrift set or the Special Guests .
The Headliner for this set is The Aetherspark , which also features a serialized version.

Vehicles are a big feature in the set. Mounts and saddle also return from Outlaws of Thunder Junction .

A major mechanic, acting as a resource , is Speed , controlled primarily by the Start your engines! ability. Your speed starts at 1, and it increases by 1 the first time an opponent loses life on each of your turns. The maximum possible speed is 4, and many cards reward achieving max speed.
A new keyword ability is Exhaust , which appears as activated abilities of permanents of various types. A given exhaust ability can only be activated once per game.

Cycling returns to act as a smoothing mechanic, and synergizes with some cards in the set that reward discarding cards or having a full graveyard. While cycling's flavor has always been a bit generic, this was a set where the name matched the theme. The cards with cycling fall into two major categories. The first are generic cyclers, letting you discard a card for another one. The second are cards that trigger an effect when you cycle them, so they play a bit more like modal cards, as you get a choice between two effects.

Cameo mechanics from Amonkhet ( Embalm , Exert ), as well as synergy with vanilla creatures (referencing Muraganda Petroglyphs ), are present in small amounts to flavorfully accent the planes on which the race is staged. No mechanics from Hour of Devastation or Kaladesh block are featured in the main set.

Aetherdrift introduces the Seal creature type. Robot is used for the first time in-universe. This is because the Guidelight Voyagers are all made fully of metal and animated by programming, rather than magic like most Constructs .

Aetherdrift follows Chandra Nalaar as she competes in the Ghirapur Grand Prix , a death-defying interplanar circuit race across Amonkhet , Avishkar and Muraganda . The racers come from near and far, the competition is fierce and the stakes are high, as her objective is the incredible prize only given to the race's champion: the Aetherspark . The race is disturbed by sudden dragonstorms .
The set is the third in the Dragonstorm Arc . The cards that represent the Story Spotlights in Aetherdrift are:

The death race idea had been in discussion for over a decade. It was the Omenpath idea (travel through multiple worlds) that finally helped it get made. Some of its inspirations were Death Race 2000 , Speed Racer , Wacky Races , and The Fast and the Furious . The genre entails not just a race where people race cars, but there is activity where people sabotage one another. Winning is as much about removing the competition as being the fastest.
Mark Rosewater calls it a " travelogue set ". While the mechanics are more focused on the race, the individual card designs are more focused on the scenery.

With the release of Aetherdrift , Gatherer introduced a series of Oracle changes. This was a very large sweep of errata, affecting a third of the cards in the game. Scryfall registered the following changes:
Approximately 12,000 creatures, artifacts, and enchantments received errata to use “this [characteristic]” for self-references instead of the card name.
Hundreds of legendary creatures and planeswalkers received errata to use new "shortnames" (a shortened version of the full cardname) in text.
The Affinity keyword was added to 16 cards that didn’t already have it.
And many smaller changes

The set was first teased during the 2023 Announcement Day panel at Gen Con where it was revealed that it would feature a Death Race across three planes . Two of the featured planes are planes from premier sets that have not been revisited since their debut ( Avishkar and Amonkhet ). The third plane is an existing location that has never been featured as a premier set before .

Writing for Card Kingdom , Jacob Lackner of Nizzahon Magic gave the set a "B" when ranking 2025's Limited formats. He praised unconventional win conditions, such as Push the Limit paired with Cycling or Aether Syphon based mill, but found Vehicles and Start your engines! "fell flat", and that "Red/White – was nigh unplayable" outside of Push the Limit due to a focus on these mechanics. Of the sets released in 2025 with mechanically new cards included in boosters , Aetherdrift was the lowest selling set.

Pit Automaton required errata before the set's release to prevent players from attempting to use its second ability to double the amount of mana produced by Exhaust mana abilities . This was not a question of balance but instead on the nature of mana abilities : they inherently can't be copied but would be recognized as an exhaust ability, wasting the doubling ability.
Similarly, Guidelight Pathmaker received errata to the "Then shuffle." instruction of its second ability. It was replaced with "If you search your library this way, shuffle."
Stock Up is an efficient card draw spell with the major upside of selecting from five cards. It has seen competitive success in every format where it's legal, from Standard to Vintage .

The illustration credit for all printed versions of Skysovereign, Consul Flagship ( Special Guests ) incorrectly states the artist was Kogado Studio instead of Imiri Sakabashira . The digital versions of the card on Magic Online and Magic: The Gathering Arena have the correct artist credit.
